title: What doesn't fit
hookLine: some things you met aren't for you

lines: THE OTHER HALF OF THE LOOK BACK.
cards: A book a friend lent you, its spine soft from years of rereading. They pressed it into your hands because it changed something for them. You've opened it again and again, and it won't open for you.
You don't throw it away. You don't tell your friend it's a bad book. You hand it back, and say thank you.

Yesterday asked what drew you. Today is the other half. Some of what you met this year may not be for you: a chant that sounded like someone else's song, a sit that never opened, a thinker whose pages stayed shut.
Today is about handing those back, kindly.

teach.h: NOT FOR ME IS NOT 'NOT GOOD'.
teach.b: First, not for me is not the same as not good. A practice that doesn't fit you is still whole for the people who keep it.
A dawn prayer, a string of beads, a koan, an hour of silence: some people build their lives around each. Not for me is a sentence about me. It says nothing about the practice.

teach.h: GIBRAN: THE THRESHOLD OF YOUR MIND.
teach.b: In The Prophet, Kahlil Gibran writes about what a real teacher does: "If he is indeed wise he does not bid you enter the house of his wisdom, but rather leads you to the threshold of your own mind."
This year brought you to a great many houses. Not every one was meant to be moved into. Some were meant to be visited, admired and left, the door closed gently behind you.

teach.h: NOT FOR ME CAN MEAN NOT NOW.
teach.b: Third, not for me can also mean not now. A book that won't open at one time of life sometimes opens at another. Letting something go kindly leaves the door unlocked.
Letting it go with a sneer bolts it shut.
Fourth, how to let go well. No mocking, no little story about how silly it was.
Name one thing it taught you, even if it's only what you don't need; a practice you set down can still teach you something true about yourself. That's the thank-you note tucked inside the cover.

how: People who try several practices may set some aside; doing it respectfully means not mocking the practice, and giving thanks for what it showed them.

o: practices from this year that aren't yours, set down with respect
old rules a tradition's own keepers no longer follow
practices that are flawed and best left behind for good

games.q: a friend asks about a practice you tried this year that didn't fit you. what do you say?
o: it wasn't for me, and here's one thing it taught me.
games.why: today's lesson: let it go kindly. name what it taught you, and leave the door unlocked. it may still be someone else's whole life.

practice: Bring to mind one practice or idea from this year that didn't fit you, and see it clearly, the way you'd look at a book on a friend's shelf, without arguing with it or with yourself.
Ask what it taught you, even a little, then set it down in your mind, like a borrowed book handed back. If you pray, you can give thanks for the people who keep it.

wordCard.voice: What doesn't fit. The practices and ideas from this year that aren't yours to keep, set down with respect for the people who do keep them. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: not for me. Said kindly, those three words leave the door unlocked. Until tomorrow.
